subject: Vendor billing path validation — card blockers & marketplace fallback
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Liu Chen <liuchen@thermovision.com>, procurement@thermovision.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: vendor billing path validation — next steps from today

Hi Liu (and procurement team),

Thanks again for the time today — useful call. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on so your AP team can decide on PO vs card vs marketplace: 

Recap (short):
- ThermoVision is evaluating Redwood for inference on the new ThermoVision Analytics platform (initial pilot).
- Procurement constraints: vendor vendor-creation timeline, PO approvals routed via Oracle AP, corporate card approvals limited to <$10k per month, and 1099/Vendor tax requirements.
- Marketplace interest: you asked if Redwood is available through CloudVendorHub and whether that would bypass some vendor checks.

Requested next steps (action owners):
1) Mateo: send a concise vendor onboarding checklist and a short table mapping common AP constraints to suggested paths (PO, card, marketplace). Attached: Redwood_Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf and a quick PO requirements spreadsheet.
2) Procurement: confirm your standard invoice remittance details, preferred purchase order format (PO number placement), and whether Net30 is required or Net45 common.
3) Marissa / Aditya (internal): advise on typical timeline if customer chooses Marketplace vs Direct contract (internal note: marketplace usually shortens vendor creation by ~2 weeks but has different invoicing).

Quick note on the card vs PO tradeoffs we discussed:
- Corporate card: fastest to get started if ThermoVision has a corporate card limit that can absorb initial spend; however, many enterprise AP teams will still request a vendor record for tax/auditing.
- PO route: preferred for procurement teams that need ledgering and centralized approvals — adds 1–3 weeks for vendor setup depending on Oracle / vendor forms.
- Marketplace (CloudVendorHub): often a middle ground — ThermoVision can purchase via marketplace SKU and Redwood receives payment through the marketplace; this can avoid a full vendor setup but may require marketplace billing reconciliation on your side.

If you can share the procurement contact and a copy of the standard PO email template you expect, I will mark the HubSpot deal with the likely route and next steps.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a brief matrix and the two attachments.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (555) 867-0242

Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf
Attachment: ThermoVision_PO-Requirements.xlsx
From: Liu Chen <liuchen@thermovision.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: vendor billing path validation — next steps from today

Hi Mateo,

Appreciate the summary — that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from procurement: 

1) Vendor creation: our AP requires a completed W-9 (or equivalent) and vendor profile. Typical turnaround is 7–14 business days once all docs are submitted.
2) PO formatting: PO number must be on the first page of the invoice, and the invoice needs to include our vendor code (if available). I'll attach our PO template and the vendor onboarding form.
3) Card policy: corporate card use is governed by our finance team — allowed for pilot spend up to $8k/month; anything above requires a formal PO.
4) Marketplace: we use CloudVendorHub for certain SaaS purchases. If Redwood is listed, we can do a marketplace purchase which would be treated as a purchase order on our side but paid via the marketplace flow. That typically shortens vendor negotiation.

I’ve attached the PO template (see procurement@thermovision.com attachment) and the vendor request form. I’ll also include our AP contact: Marla Singh (marla.singh@thermovision.com). Please make sure vendor tax ID is included on your onboarding doc.

Thanks — we’ll review the checklist and aim to confirm the path by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Liu Chen
Director, Platform Engineering
ThermoVision Systems

Liu — thanks for the specifics. Attaching a pared-down vendor checklist with the items tied to each AP path (PO / Card / Marketplace). A few items to call out that often change the decision:

- Thresholds: you mentioned $8k/month card limit — that puts initial pilot squarely in 'card' for month 1, but if pilot ramps quickly we should be ready to convert to PO.
- Tax/Vendor ID: we will include our EIN/Tax ID on the onboarding form (attached).
- Invoice delivery: Redwood can send invoices to invoices@thermovision.com or via CloudVendorHub depending on your preference.

Proposed micro-plan:
1) Pilot month 0 (first 30 days): thermovision uses corporate card to avoid vendor setup delay.
2) If pilot metrics exceed $10k projected spend in month 2, open the vendor creation + PO path in parallel (we will submit W-9 and onboarding form immediately).
3) If ThermoVision prefers marketplace, we’ll fast-track a CloudVendorHub listing conversation (Marissa, Aditya — can you confirm Redwood’s current marketplace status and estimated listing lead time?).

Marissa / Aditya — can you confirm: 
- Redwood listing status on CloudVendorHub (green/amber/red) and expected days to list.
- Whether Redwood can accept invoice delivery to a marketplace remittance email.

Liu — I’ll also add Marla Singh to the thread if that’s OK so we can capture precise AP routing.

Thanks,
Mateo

Adding Marla — hi Marla, great to e-meet you. Quick internal note on marketplace status: Redwood is currently listed on CloudVendorHub with a standard SaaS SKU; typical listing-to-live is 10–14 business days once we approve the marketplace legal terms. If ThermoVision wants immediate access, the fastest route is Mateo’s suggested approach: start with corporate card for the first month while we kick off vendor creation and parallel marketplace listing.

We will:
